summary: Web threads show read failures instead of hiding them behind old rows, mark a section 'Updates paused' once until the gateway is live again, and pin agent and mission threads as one collapsed summary whose rows open the thread in its own tab

replay.detail: The web client reads the same thread list, detail and timeline endpoints; no history is replayed or rebuilt.

schema.detail: No storage, wire or generated-schema change. The browser keeps drafts and retained first sends in the same places.

rules.detail: Thread grants, browser send grants and the ordinary/thread delivery policy are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Web only, against the same daemons as before. After a thread read has succeeded, only a lost path to Fractal (a network failure, or a gateway answering 502, 503 or 504) keeps the observed rows, marked paused. A malformed or mismatched response, a 404 and other HTTP errors now replace them with 'Fractal could not load threads.' and Retry, and are logged as 'Thread read failed'; the one exception is a thread opened in its own tab that Fractal answers not-found, which says 'Fractal has no thread at this link.' without Retry. Refusals replace them with their reason and offer neither Start nor Retry. A rejected browser credential uses the shared 'Access revoked' sentence. 'Updates paused' appears once at the section heading (or above a thread in its own tab) and stays until the gateway connection is live again. A thread send refused because Fractal could not be reached clears its advice once the gateway is live again, keeping the draft. Agent and mission views show a collapsed 'Threads, N' summary; its rows open the thread tab rather than expanding in place, and on a phone the tab row scrolls to show the selected tab. The Inbox start draft opens under the Threads heading with a 'Thread title' field and a 'To <agent>' line, and is offered again as 'Continue draft'. Close, reopen and rename events read as one muted line; the 'Sending…' line under the editor is removed; a connection without the reply grant shows a read-only note where the composer was. Before Fractal has answered which operations the browser holds, the conversation composer says it is checking whether this browser can send instead of 'Message send is not granted for this device.', and the browser pairing offer waits for that answer.

downtime.detail: Refreshing the web bundle does not interrupt the daemon.

manual.detail: No operator step. Reviewing against real data still uses the connected threads preview described in docs/fractal-web.md; the Storybook stories remain local fixtures.

recovery.detail: A failed read recovers through its Retry or the next successful read; a revoked browser pairs again. Rolling the web bundle back restores the previous presentation; drafts, retained first sends and pairing are preserved.
